label: rem:mass-modulus-em-phase-color-grading
title: Mass is the modulus, electromagnetism the phase, color the $S_3$ grading of one trace
html:
The factorization of prop:color-spacetime-s5-factorization fixes how the three observables of a Bring-embeddable knot sit on the single trace scalar \mathrm{tr}_M and its trace algebra H_2(q)\oplus H_3(q).

Three readings of one trace

We write the trace scalar in polar form:

  \mathrm{tr}_M \;=\; \lVert\mathrm{tr}_M\rVert\,\exp\!\big(i\,\arg\mathrm{tr}_M\big).

This forms the multiplicative companion of the additive complex-volume reconstruction \mathrm{Re}\mathfrak{V}+i\mathrm{Im}\mathfrak{V}=\mathfrak{V} (conj:binding-qbeta-complex-volume). We then have:

reading quantity sector character
mass modulus \lVert\mathrm{tr}_M\rVert both nonnegative magnitude
electromagnetism argument \arg\mathrm{tr}_M spacetime / S_2 continuous U(1)
color S_3 irrep grading color / S_3 discrete

Mass evaluates the magnitude that survives both sectors. The argument evaluates the continuous U(1) framing/Chern–Simons phase. This provides the \mathrm{Im}\mathfrak{V} channel, picked up as the ribbon twist q^{2w\,c(\lambda)} on a framed knot of writhe w (bar-parity-split). It lives in the spacetime block, where we read it as the electromagnetic phase. Color provides the discrete grading of the algebra element across the H_3(q) representations, before the trace collapses it to a scalar.

Color is not the phase

The color factor S_3 fixes the spacetime coordinates. The spacetime factor S_2 fixes the color coordinates (prop:color-spacetime-s5-factorization, parts 1–2). Therefore, color and electromagnetism form independent coordinates. The discrete color charge is not a function of the continuous phase, and conversely. The rigidity in part 3 of that proposition makes this non-coincidence sharp. A continuous winding argument cannot factor through a finite group such as \mu_5. Thus, \arg\mathrm{tr}_M remains structurally barred from being a color character.

The two remain nonetheless faces of one substrate. The Galois group S_5 properly contains S_2\times S_3. Its remaining generators carry spacetime indices into color indices. An electromagnetic-to-color relation therefore forms an S_5 statement, realized by those off-block generators, not a relation internal to the U(1) phase.

Archimedean realization

The polar split provides the archimedean reading. The modulus and argument require the realization of the trace over \mathbb{C}, on the far side of the substrate-to-archimedean wall. The structural content of prop:color-spacetime-s5-factorization—the faithful S_2\times S_3\hookrightarrow S_5 embedding, the orthogonality of the two sectors, and the divisibility rigidity—is generic and requires no such realization.

Relation to the literature

The individual ingredients form classical results. The imaginary partner of a hyperbolic volume forms a Chern–Simons invariant (Neumann–Zagier [neumann-zagier1985]). The colored-Jones asymptotics realize this complex volume at roots of unity (Volume Conjecture [kashaev1997, murakami-murakami2001]). The Jones polynomial forms a Chern–Simons expectation value whose framing dependence produces the U(1) phase (Witten [witten1989], Reshetikhin–Turaev [reshetikhin1991]). The complexified continuation of the phase forms Witten [witten2011], and the bar-involution structure of the root-of-unity asymptotics forms the quantum-modularity of Zagier [zagier2010]. The quantum dilogarithm controlling the asymptotics forms Faddeev–Kashaev [faddeev1994].

Read against this work, two of our identifications constitute recombinations and two are specific to this framework. The reading modulus/argument = volume/Chern–Simons and the placement of the argument as a U(1) framing phase restate the cited results. The identification of the modulus with mass \lVert\mathrm{tr}_M\rVert and of color with the S_3\subset S_5 representation grading of the Bring quintic's Galois group are our own. The literature offers the nearby A_5 / S_5 flavor and modular-flavor symmetries rather than this trace-algebra grading. Our contribution forms the group-theoretic statement that these three readings are orthogonal sectors of one trace object, alongside the rigidity barring the continuous phase from being the discrete color charge.

Classical antecedents of the involutive reading

Resolving one object into observables under an involution is a recurring structure. Four classical instances frame ours:

  • Frobenius–Schur indicator. The character involution \chi\mapsto\chi(g^{-1}) [frobenius-schur1906]—the bar-involution q\mapsto q^{-1} on the Hecke side—sorts every irreducible representation as real, quaternionic, or complex. The bar-even (binding, \cosh) and bar-odd (\beta-decay, \sinh) channels construct the rank-one shadow of this trichotomy on the trace.
  • Modular conjugation. The Markov trace forms a trace on a finite von Neumann algebra [jones1985]. Every such algebra carries the Tomita–Takesaki modular conjugation J and modular operator \Delta [takesaki1970]. The observable elements are the J-fixed (self-adjoint) ones, and a=\tfrac12(a+a^*)+\tfrac12(a-a^*) forms the algebra-level bar-parity split. The polar reading (mass =\lVert\mathrm{tr}_M\rVert, phase =\arg\mathrm{tr}_M) provides its modulus–modular-flow form.
  • Weil operator. On a polarized Hodge structure, the Weil operator [weil1958] supplies the complex structure packaging real harmonic periods into a polarized complex period. The complex volume \mathrm{Vol}+i\,\mathrm{CS} [neumann-zagier1985] provides such a period, and H^1(\mathrm{Bring})=2W forms such a structure—the Hodge-theoretic home of the complex-volume half.
  • Conjugate-variable amplitude. The oscillator amplitude a=q+ip combines a canonically conjugate pair through the symplectic complex structure, with \lVert a\rVert^2 the energy and \arg a the phase.

In physics, this reading follows the complex-energy / resonance tradition. A state forms a complex pole \mathfrak{E}=\mathfrak{m}-i\Gamma/2 (Gamow [gamow1928], Breit–Wigner [breit-wigner1936]) whose real part gives mass and whose imaginary part gives decay width. The bound sector lies on the conjugation-fixed real axis, and the optical theorem ties the imaginary part to the total decay rate. The Kramers–Kronig dispersion relations [kronig1926] lock the reactive (real) and absorptive (imaginary) parts of one causal response. There, the involution is complex conjugation / time reversal. Here, the bar-involution q\mapsto q^{-1} plays that role at the fibre level. We claim not the involutive reading itself, but its realization on the categorical knot trace, where \mathrm{Im}(q_0)=0 at the archimedean level renders the two parts separately real observable shadows.
